head: claude/night-shift-telegram-ping
title: queue the night-shift summary to the Telegram bot (and what the trace says about the delivery defect)
body:
## Summary

Queues the night-shift summary as a **high**-priority ping to `target: "claude"` (@claude_ict_comms_bot, per CLAUDE.md's two-bot separation — trade alerts keep the `trader` target).

**One line appended to `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl`.** Nothing else touched.

## ⚠️ This PR is the ONLY thing standing between that ping and Telegram

The operator asked for this to reach the Telegram bot. Traced end to end, the delivery path is:

```
docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl   (committed — this PR)
  → merge to main
  → ict-git-sync pulls on the VM (~5 min timer)
  → notify_on_pull.py drains the row, send_ping.enqueue(target="claude")
  → writes runtime_logs/pending_claude_pings/  (VM-local, gitignored)
  → the bot drains that dir and POSTs to Telegram
```

**A merge to `main` is step 2 of 6.** Until this merges, the row reaches nothing. The night-manager session cannot merge it — `update_pull_request` 403s on both `draft` and `title`, and `pr-opener.yml` creates every PR as a draft regardless of `"draft": false` in the request.

**No direct send was possible.** `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` and `CLAUDE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` are all unset in the session container, so there is no path that bypasses the queue.

## What this incidentally confirms about the delivery defect

`BL-20260902-PING-DELIVERY-IS-MARKED-ON-A-LOCAL-FILE-WRITE-SO-DELIVERED-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE` says `_post_telegram` is "defined and NEVER CALLED". **Read literally that is false** — `_post_telegram` *is* called, by `_send_priority` at `scripts/notify_on_pull.py:139`. **In substance it is correct**: `_send_priority` itself has **zero callers**, so the whole Telegram transport in that module is dead code, orphaned when S-019 moved delivery to the bot's inbox. `main()` calls `send_ping.enqueue(...)` and then `_record_delivered_hash(...)` — so a recorded "delivered" hash attests **a local file write**, never a Telegram 200.

The row's substance stands and it should not be closed on the technicality; the wording is worth tightening to "orphaned — its only caller has no callers" so a future reader does not disprove it in one grep and dismiss it.

## The ping's own text is honest about this

It tells the operator, in the message body: *"If you are reading this in Telegram, THAT is the first observed end-to-end delivery. If you are not, that is the defect."* Nobody has yet observed a ping reaching the operator; everything green so far proves only that pings were **queued**.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — one appended JSONL row. No schema, boundary, pipeline, deployment, runtime, API or config change.

## Test plan

- [x] All **60** rows in `pending-pings.jsonl` parse as JSON after the append (population stated: the whole file, not just the new row)
- [x] `scripts/ci/check_pending_pings_render.py` → `OK — all 60 queued ping(s) render a body` — the new row renders, so it cannot be a body-less silent drop
- [x] Diff is exactly `1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)` — appended as raw text, never re-serialised
- [x] `target: "claude"` is correct per the two-bot separation; the `trader` target is untouched
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] ⚠️ **NOT verified and cannot be from here: that the ping actually arrives.** That needs this merged, the VM to pull, and the bot to drain. Tier-1 to queue; the VM-side transport is Tier-2.

## Filed for follow-ups

- **#10859 remains held** on the operator's one Tier-2 OK. Untouched.
- The delivery defect itself is **not fixed here** — this PR uses the existing path, it does not repair it.
